messages.subject: inprod in OpenBUGS and Nimble
parts:
In this likelihood mu calculated by hand and with inprod give the same posterior means in OpenBUGS but different posterior means in Nimble. Why does Nimble appear to treat these two expressions differently, and which is the correct expression to use in Nimble?

for (i in 1:n){
      y[i] ~ dnorm( mu[i], tau )
     mu[i] <- gb[1]*x[i,1] + gb[2]*x[i,2] + gb[3]*x[i,3] + gb[4]*x[i,4] + gb[5]*x[i,5]
    #mu[i] <- inprod(x[i,], gb[] )
}
